109:3:1.a: I’d say that it was more profitable to deal in cars.

109:3:2.q: Why? Can you tell me the name of one of your local car dealers?
109:3:2.a: Yes, I can tell you the name of one of my local car dealers: Johnson Motors.

109:3:3.q: What do we call the person who deals the cards in a game of poker?
109:3:3.a: We call the person who deals the cards in a game of poker the dealer or the banker.

109:3:4.q: What do we mean when we say we make a deal with someone?
109:3:4.a: When we say we make a deal with someone, we mean we agree to give someone something in return for something they will give us, or to do something for someone in return for something they will do for us.

109:5:0.q: Do you think you could run a large factory, or don't you think you could even run a small coffee shop?
109:5:0.a: I think I could run a large factory.

109:6:0.q: What words can we use when we want to emphasize the person who does the action in a particular sentence?
109:6:0.a: When we want to emphasize the person who does the action in a particular sentence, we can use “myself”, “yourself”, “himself” etc.

109:6:1.q: What do we call these words?
109:6:1.a: We call these words emphasizing pronouns.

109:6:3.q: Does someone else usually make breakfast for you or do you make it yourself?

109:6:4.q: What’s the difference between these two sentences: “He painted the house himself” and “He painted the house by himself”?
109:6:4.a: The difference between these two sentences is that the first sentence emphasizes the fact that he painted the house, not someone else, whereas the second sentence means he painted the house alone, without any help.

109:6:5.q: Does this door shut by itself?
109:6:5.a: Yes, this door shuts by itself.

109:6:6.q: Do students answer questions in these lessons by themselves?
109:6:6.a: No, students don’t answer questions in these lessons by themselves; the teacher helps them to answer.

109:7:0.q: Have you ever been anywhere in the world that was so hot that you couldn’t stand the heat?
109:7:0.a: Yes, I’ve been to Dubai, where it was so hot that I couldn’t stand the heat.

109:7:1.q: Give me an example of something that you can’t stand.
109:7:1.a: I can’t stand people talking loudly in the cinema.

109:8:1.q: What does the idiom “get a move on” mean?
109:8:1.a: The idiom “get a move on” means “hurry”.

110:0:0.q: Are there any mountains in your country where snow settles on the top even in the middle of summer?
110:0:0.a: Yes, there are some mountains in my country where snow settles on the top even in the middle of summer.

110:0:1.q: Where? Would you be surprised if you were walking across a park and a bird came and settled on your shoulder?
110:0:1.a: Yes, I’d be surprised if I were walking across a park and a bird came and settled on my shoulder.

110:0:2.q: Would you find it difficult to settle in a foreign country forever?
110:0:2.a: Yes, I’d find it difficult to settle in a foreign country forever.

110:0:3.q: Why or why not? If you couldn’t settle your bill in a restaurant because you didn’t have enough money with you, what would you do?
110:0:3.a: If I couldn’t settle my bill in a restaurant because I didn’t have enough money with me, I’d call a friend and ask them to bring me some money.

110:0:4.q: When you add sugar to a cup of coffee, what happens if you don’t stir it?
110:0:4.a: When you add sugar to a cup of coffee and don’t stir it, the sugar settles to the bottom of the cup.

110:0:5.q: If two countries can't settle a political problem, where do they go in order to settle it?
110:0:5.a: If two countries can’t settle a political problem, they go to the United Nations (UN) in order to settle it.

110:0:6.q: What does a teacher say to pupils when they are making too much noise?
110:0:6.a: A teacher says “Come on now, settle down” to pupils when they are making too much noise.

110:0:7.q: If someone said that they were planning to go on holiday but that nothing had been settled yet, what would they mean?
110:0:7.a: If someone said that they were planning to go on holiday but that nothing had been settled yet, they would mean that they had not made any final decisions yet.

110:1:0.q: Would you say that success in life was partly a question of luck?
110:1:0.a: Yes, I’d say that success in life was partly a question of luck.

110:2:0.q: Do soldiers have to be extremely brave when they go into battle?
110:2:0.a: Yes, soldiers have to be extremely brave when they go into battle.

110:3:2.q: Is it often difficult for parents to get their children to tidy their rooms?
110:3:2.a: Yes, it’s often difficult for parents to get their children to tidy their rooms.

110:4:0.q: Have you ever acted on the stage in the theatre?
110:4:0.a: No, I’ve never acted on the stage in the theatre.

110:4:1.q: When? Would you be afraid to act on the stage?
110:4:1.a: Yes, I’d be afraid to act on the stage.

110:4:2.q: At what stage of your English studies are you at the moment: beginner, intermediate or advanced?
110:4:2.a: I’m at an intermediate stage in my English studies at the moment.

110:5:1.q: If you followed a river upstream, where would it eventually lead you to?
110:5:1.a: If you followed a river upstream, it’d eventually lead you to the mountains or hills.

110:5:2.q: And if you followed it downstream, where would it eventually lead you to?
110:5:2.a: If you followed a river downstream, it’d eventually lead you to the sea or a lake.

110:5:3.q: If you saw a stream of people streaming out of a building in a hurry, what'd you think?
110:5:3.a: If I saw a stream of people streaming out of a building in a hurry, I’d think that either the building was on fire or that the people had just finished work.

110:6:0.q: What are the two types of relative clause?
110:6:0.a: The two types of relative clause are defining relative clauses and non-defining relative clauses.

110:6:1.q: What’s the difference between a defining relative clause and a non- defining relative clause?
110:6:1.a: The difference between a defining relative clause and a non-defining relative clause is that a defining relative clause identifies which person or thing we are talking about, whereas a non-defining relative clause simply gives us extra information about them.

110:6:4.q: How is a non-defining clause separated from the main part of the sentence?
110:6:4.a: A non-defining clause is separated from the main part of the sentence by commas.

110:6:5.q: When can we use the relative pronoun “that” instead of “who” or “which”?
110:6:5.a: We can use the relative pronoun “that” instead of “who” or “which” in defining clauses; we cannot use “that” in non-defining clauses.

110:6:7.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence, please: London, that is the capital of England, is a big city.
110:6:7.a: London, which is the capital of England, is a big city.

110:7:1.q: What does the idiom “for good” mean?

111:0:1.q: What happens to the branch of a tree when it waves too much in the wind?
111:0:1.a: When the branch waves too much in the wind, it breaks and falls to the ground.

111:0:3.q: Is it pleasant to travel by boat when the waves of the sea are very high?
111:0:3.a: No, it isn’t pleasant to travel by boat when the waves of the sea are very high.

111:0:5.q: Do you prefer wavy hair rather than straight hair?
111:0:5.a: Yes, I prefer wavy hair rather than straight hair.

111:1:0.q: What do you recommend that people do in order to succeed in life?
111:1:0.a: I recommend that people work hard in order to succeed in life.

111:1:1.q: Which film would you recommend seeing at the cinema at the moment?
111:1:1.a: I’d recommend seeing Dune at the cinema at the moment.

111:1:2.q: If someone said they wanted a quiet holiday, which part of this country would you recommend to them?
111:1:2.a: If someone said they wanted a quiet holiday, I’d recommend the Lake District to them.

111:3:0.q: What, generally speaking, is the difference between an injury and a wound?
111:3:0.a: Generally speaking, the difference between an injury and a wound is that we use “injury” for physical damage caused by an accident and “wound” for an injury in which the skin is cut or broken.

111:3:1.q: Have you ever seen anyone badly injured as the result of an accident?
111:3:1.a: No, I’ve never seen anyone badly injured as the result of an accident.

111:3:2.q: Do you know anyone who has been wounded in a war?
111:3:2.a: No, I don’t know anyone who has been wounded in a war.

111:3:3.q: Are your feelings easily wounded (or hurt)?
111:3:3.a: No, my feelings aren’t easily wounded.

111:4:0.q: What do we mean if we say that somebody is not being sincere?
111:4:0.a: If we say that somebody is not being sincere, we mean that they are not expressing their true feelings.

111:5:0.q: Have you ever done any voluntary work?
111:5:0.a: Yes, I’ve done voluntary work at a local animal shelter.

111:5:1.q: Do you think children ought to be made to study, or do you think studying ought to be voluntary?
111:5:1.a: I think children ought to be made to study.

111:7:0.a: The difference between “separate” as a verb and “separate” as an adjective is that “separate” pronounced /ˈsepəreɪt/ is the verb and “separate” pronounced /ˈsepərət/ is the adjective.

111:8:0.q: How do we begin a formal letter or email if we don’t know the name of the person we’re writing to?
111:8:0.a: We begin a formal letter or email with the words “Dear Sir” or “Dear Madam” if we don’t know the name of the person we’re writing to.

111:8:1.q: How do we generally end such a letter or email?
111:8:1.a: We generally end such a letter or email with the words “Yours faithfully”.

111:8:2.q: If we know the name of the person we are writing to, how do we begin a formal letter or email?
111:8:2.a: If we know the name of the person we are writing to, we begin a formal letter or email with “Dear” followed by the person’s title and surname.

111:8:3.q: And how do we end such a letter?
111:8:3.a: We end such a letter with the words “Yours sincerely”.

111:8:4.q: How do we usually begin an informal letter or email?
111:8:4.a: We usually begin an informal letter or email with “Dear” followed by the person’s first name.

111:8:5.q: And how can we end such a letter or email?
111:8:5.a: We can end such a letter or email with the words “Best wishes”.

111:9:1.q: If we are answering a formal letter, how do we often begin our letter?
111:9:1.a: If we are answering a formal letter, we often begin our letter with “With reference to your letter of 19th January, I am writing to provide the information you requested.”

111:10:1.q: If you order goods online but they don't arrive, can you cancel the order and get a refund?
111:10:1.a: Yes, if I order goods online but they don’t arrive, I can cancel the order and get a refund.

111:11:0.q: How do we know when a dog is in good condition?
111:11:0.a: We know a dog is in good condition when its coat is shining and its nose is cold and wet.

111:11:2.q: Do you think that people should have the right to strike?
111:11:2.a: Yes, I think that people should have the right to strike.

111:12:0.q: When you post a letter, do you take it to a post office or do you just put it in the nearest postbox?
111:12:0.a: When I post a letter, I just put it in the nearest postbox.

111:13:0.q: If you can't manage to answer a question, what does the teacher do?
111:13:0.a: If I can’t manage to answer a question, the teacher helps me.

111:14:0.q: Which do you think it's better to possess: brains, beauty or money?
111:14:0.a: I think it’s better to possess brains than beauty or money.

111:17:1.q: What does the idiom “just the job” mean?
111:17:1.a: The idiom “just the job” means “exactly what is needed”.

112:0:0.q: Do you like people who are always laughing and joking?
112:0:0.a: Yes, I like people who are always laughing and joking.

112:1:1.q: When children play together, do they often pretend to be adults?
112:1:1.a: Yes, when children play together, they often pretend to be adults.

112:1:2.q: If you see someone you know in the street but you’re in too much of a hurry to stop and say hello, do you sometimes pretend not to notice them?
112:1:2.a: Yes, if I see someone I know in the street but I’m in too much of a hurry to stop and say hello, I sometimes pretend not to notice them.

112:2:0.q: What do we have to put on an envelope before posting a letter?
112:2:0.a: We have to put an address and a stamp on an envelope before posting a letter.

112:2:1.q: If you write the address on the envelope but leave out the postcode, will the letter still arrive?
112:2:1.a: Yes, if you write the address on the envelope but leave out the postcode, the letter will still arrive, but it may take longer.

112:3:0.q: Would you find it difficult to behave naturally if you met someone really famous?
112:3:0.a: Yes, I’d find it difficult to behave naturally if I met someone really famous.

112:3:1.q: What do I mean if I say “Naturally, she was pleased about passing the test“?
112:3:1.a: If you say “Naturally, she was pleased about passing the test”, you mean “Of course, she was pleased about passing the test”.

112:4:0.q: What is the most recent film you have seen?
112:4:0.a: The most recent film I have seen is Titanic.

112:4:1.q: What was it like – that is, was it good, bad, or just so-so?

112:4:2.q: Have you been to any concerts recently?
112:4:2.a: Yes, I’ve been to a rock concert recently.

112:5:0.q: What can we say instead of the word “friend“ in very informal English?
112:5:0.a: We can say “mate” instead of the word “friend” in very informal English.

112:5:2.q: Do you know the names of all your classmates?
112:5:2.a: Yes, I know the names of all my classmates.

112:5:3.q: If you thought one of your workmates was stealing money from the company you worked for, what would you do?
112:5:3.a: If I thought one of my workmates was stealing money from the company I worked for, I’d report them to the manager.

112:6:0.q: Is there anything you’re really looking forward to doing at the moment?
112:6:0.a: Yes, there’s something I’m really looking forward to doing at the moment.

112:6:1.q: What? What kind of things do you look forward to most?
112:6:1.a: The kind of things I look forward to most are holidays and spending time with my friends.

112:7:0.q: What does the expression “Let me see“ mean?
112:7:0.a: The expression “Let me see” means “Give me time to think for a minute”.

112:8:0.q: If you were the owner of a business and one of your workers stole something from the business, would you give them a second chance, or would you dismiss them at once?
112:8:0.a: If I were the owner of a business and one of my workers stole something from the business, I’d dismiss them at once.

112:8:1.q: Why? Supposing there was a place, shall we say, somewhere in the middle of a jungle in South America, where you knew for sure that there was about fifty million pounds’ worth of gold, but the chances of returning alive were only fifty-fifty, would you go and take a chance and try your luck, or would you just stay at home and dream about it?
112:8:1.a: Supposing there was a place somewhere in the middle of a jungle in South America where I knew for sure that there was about fifty million pounds’ worth of gold, but the chances of returning alive were only fifty-fifty, I’d stay at home and dream about it.

112:10:0.q: Many years ago, did humans have to hunt animals for food?
112:10:0.a: Yes, many years ago, humans had to hunt animals for food.

112:11:0.q: Why should we judge a person by his deeds more than by his words?
112:11:0.a: We should judge a person by his deeds more than by his words because it’s easier to say things than to do them.

112:12:0.q: What do we use grease for?
112:12:0.a: We use grease to make the different parts of a machine move smoothly.

112:14:0.q: If you were in a bus going downhill and the driver suddenly lost control of the bus, what’d you do?
112:14:0.a: If I were in a bus going downhill and the driver suddenly lost control of the bus, I’d try to take control of the bus.

112:15:0.q: What might happen if you didn’t pay your electricity bill when it was due?
112:15:0.a: If I didn’t pay my electricity bill when it was due, they might come and cut the electricity off until I paid it.

112:15:1.q: When are you due to come here again?
112:15:1.a: I’m due to come here again next Monday.

112:15:2.q: Why don’t trains always arrive when they are due?
112:15:2.a: Trains don’t always arrive when they are due because of bad weather and breakdowns.

112:15:3.q: When a person is rich, do you think it’s due to the fact that they’re more intelligent than most other people, or do you think it’s mainly due to luck?
112:15:3.a: When a person is rich, I think it’s mainly due to luck.

112:16:0.q: Were your grandmothers both born in the same country as you?
112:16:0.a: Yes, my grandmothers were both born in the same country as me.

112:16:1.q: What do we call our grandfather’s father?
112:16:1.a: We call our grandfather’s father our great-grandfather.

112:17:0.q: Are the people in this country mostly tea drinkers or coffee drinkers?
112:17:0.a: The people in this country are mostly tea drinkers.

112:17:1.q: Do you think that passing exams is mostly a question of luck?
112:17:1.a: No, I don’t think that passing exams is mostly a question of luck.

112:18:0.q: Do you think your language is totally different from English?
112:18:0.a: No, I don’t think my language is totally different from English.

112:18:1.q: If a friend of yours is wearing clothes that look totally wrong on them, do you tell them?
112:18:1.a: Yes, if a friend of mine is wearing clothes that look totally wrong on them, I tell them.

112:19:1.q: What does the idiom “let yourself go” mean?
112:19:1.a: The idiom “let yourself go” means “relax and behave freely”.

113:0:0.q: What’s the difference between “to discuss”, “to argue“ and “to quarrel“?
113:0:0.a: The difference between “to discuss”, “to argue” and “to quarrel” is that “to discuss” means to talk about something calmly, “to argue” means to disagree badly with someone, and “to quarrel” means to lose control and shout angrily at someone.

113:0:2.q: Why do housemates sometimes argue with one another?
113:0:2.a: Housemates sometimes argue with one another because they disagree about cleaning and paying the bills.

113:0:3.q: Did you quarrel a lot with your brother or sister when you were a child?
113:0:3.a: Yes, I quarrelled a lot with my brother when I was a child.

113:1:1.q: Would you say that a regular life was better than an irregular one?
113:1:1.a: Yes, I’d say that a regular life was better than an irregular one.

113:1:2.q: Why or why not? Can a dentist do anything about irregular teeth?
113:1:2.a: Yes, a dentist can straighten irregular teeth with braces.

113:1:3.q: Do you work (or study) irregular hours?
113:1:3.a: No, I don’t study irregular hours.

113:2:0.q: Why is it important to blow up bridges during a war?
113:2:0.a: It’s important to blow up bridges during a war in order to make it difficult for the enemy to get across the river; to do so, they would either have to swim, cross by boat or build new bridges.

113:3:1.q: Have you ever collected stamps or anything like that?

113:3:3.q: Do they collect money in the streets in your country for different causes, such as for the Red Cross, the poor etc.?
113:3:3.a: Yes, they collect money in the streets in my country for different causes.

113:3:4.q: What do you consider to be a good cause worth collecting money for?
113:3:4.a: I consider helping poor children to be a good cause worth collecting money for.

113:4:0.q: What kind of furniture do you like to see a room furnished with?
113:4:0.a: I like to see a room furnished with comfortable, modern furniture.

113:5:0.q: How long does it usually take for a new film to become available to buy?
113:5:0.a: It usually takes a few months for a new film to become available to buy.

113:5:1.q: If you rang somebody up when they were at work but they weren’t available immediately, would you wait, leave a message or call back later?
113:5:1.a: If I rang somebody up when they were at work but they weren’t available immediately, I’d leave a message.

113:6:0.q: Do you think that human beings sometimes behave worse than animals?
113:6:0.a: Yes, I think that human beings sometimes behave worse than animals.

113:8:0.q: When do we add the letters “es” to form the plural of a noun and the third person singular of a verb?
113:8:0.a: We add the letters “es” when a word ends in the letters “o”, “s”, “x”, “z”, “ch” or “sh”.

113:8:2.q: What happens when a noun or verb ends in a consonant plus “y“?
113:8:2.a: When a noun or verb ends in a consonant plus “y”, the “y” is changed to “i” and then the letters “es” are added.

113:8:4.q: If you kiss your mother hello, how many kisses do you give her – one, two or three?
113:8:4.a: If I kiss my mother hello, I give her two kisses.

113:8:5.q: What do we mean by the rush hour in a large city?
113:8:5.a: By the rush hour in a large city, we mean the time when everyone rushes to work or home from work.

113:8:6.q: Who were your heroes when you were a child?
113:8:6.a: My heroes when I was a child were my parents.

113:9:1.q: What does the idiom “pull someone’s leg” mean?
113:9:1.a: The idiom “pull someone’s leg” means “joke with someone by making them believe something that is not true”.

114:0:0.q: What’s the difference between a dish and a plate?
114:0:0.a: The difference between a dish and a plate is that a dish is a container used for serving food, whereas a plate is a flat dish from which we eat.

114:0:1.a: My favourite dish is spaghetti bolognese.

114:0:2.q: Do you know how to make it?
114:0:2.a: Yes, I know how to make it.

114:1:0.q: Are you for or against the police carrying arms when they’re walking around the streets on duty?
114:1:0.a: I’m for the police carrying arms when they’re walking around the streets on duty.

114:1:1.q: Why? Are you for or against fox hunting?
114:1:1.a: I’m against fox hunting because it’s cruel.

114:2:0.q: What do members of the general public do when they see a criminal seize a woman’s handbag in the street?
114:2:0.a: When members of the general public see a criminal seize a woman’s handbag in the street, some run after the criminal or shout for help, but most people just stand and look too surprised to do anything.

114:3:0.q: What would you do if another world war broke out?
114:3:0.a: If another world war broke out, I’d try to move somewhere safe.

114:4:0.a: The difference between a wage and a salary is that a wage is usually paid weekly, whereas a salary is usually paid monthly.

114:5:0.q: What kind of people don’t earn a steady wage or salary?
114:5:0.a: The kind of people who don’t earn a steady wage or salary are actors, artists, writers etc.

114:5:1.q: Do seasonal workers, such as waiters who work at seaside hotels in the summer, receive a wage or a salary?

114:5:3.q: About how long do you think it’ll take you to finish this book if you keep working steadily?
114:5:3.a: I think it’ll take me about six months to finish this book.

114:6:0.q: How do we generally form the plural of a noun ending in “f“ or “fe“?
114:6:0.a: We generally form the plural of a noun ending in “f” or “fe” by changing the “f” or “fe” to “ves“.

114:6:1.a: Leaf – leaves, knife – knives, wife – wives.

114:6:2.q: What are three common exceptions to this rule?
114:6:2.a: Three common exceptions to this rule are “chefs”, “cliffs” and “roofs”.

114:8:0.q: What kind of things do people often mention when they’re telling you about a holiday they’ve just been on?
114:8:0.a: People often mention the weather, the food etc. when they’re telling you about a holiday they’ve just been on.

114:9:0.q: When does a mother tell off her child?
114:9:0.a: A mother tells off her child when the child has done something wrong and made her angry.

114:10:0.q: If you went into business, would you prefer to have a partner or to be alone?
114:10:0.a: If I went into business, I’d prefer to have a partner.

114:11:0.q: If a friend buys you a drink in a bar, do you normally insist on giving them the money or do you just buy them a drink the next time?
114:11:0.a: If a friend buys me a drink in a bar, I just buy them a drink the next time.

114:12:0.q: What’s the basic meaning of the word “board“?
114:12:0.a: The basic meaning of the word “board” is a flat piece of wood.

114:12:1.q: Give me some examples of what we get from the word “board“.
114:12:1.a: Some examples of what we get from the word “board” are “floorboard“, “noticeboard” etc.

114:12:3.q: Do you have to show your passport before you can board a plane?
114:12:3.a: Yes, I have to show my passport before I can board a plane.

114:12:4.q: What would happen if you went on board ship to say goodbye to a friend and you remained on board after the ship had left port?
114:12:4.a: If I went on board ship to say goodbye to a friend and remained on board after the ship had left port, I’d have to leave the ship at the next available port.

114:12:5.q: What do we mean by a “board of directors“?
114:12:5.a: By a “board of directors” we mean a group of people who manage a company.

114:12:6.q: What do we mean by a “board meeting“?
114:12:6.a: By a “board meeting” we mean a meeting of company directors round a table.

114:12:7.q: If you stayed at a hotel on holiday, would you choose “full board“, “half board“ or “bed and breakfast“?
114:12:7.a: If I stayed at a hotel on holiday, I’d choose full board.

114:13:1.q: What does the idiom “see eye to eye” mean?
114:13:1.a: The idiom “see eye to eye” means “agree with someone”.

115:0:1.a: This lesson finishes at twelve o’clock.

115:0:2.q: Do you know when your local football team play their next game?
115:0:2.a: Yes, I know when my local football team play their next game.

115:1:0.q: Give us a short account of what you did yesterday.
115:1:0.a: Yesterday, I went to work, had dinner with my family, and watched television.

115:1:1.q: Give us a short account of the last film you saw.

137:8:0.q: If you had left for Scotland ten hours ago, would you have arrived there by now?

137:10:0.q: In ancient history, did the conquerors of a country usually show mercy to the people of the country they had conquered?

137:12:0.q: If you developed an ache in your lower back that would not go away, would you ignore it or go to the doctor?
137:12:0.a: If I developed an ache in my lower back that would not go away, I’d go to the doctor.

137:13:0.q: Why is it healthier to sit and walk upright rather than with one’s head and shoulders bent forward?
137:13:0.a: The reason it’s healthier to sit and walk upright rather than with one’s head and shoulders bent forward is that the lungs and other organs of the body are not pressed against each other, and, with an upright back, the blood moves more freely in the body and the person feels less tired.

137:14:2.q: Does it often rain in the south of Spain?

137:16:0.a: Yes, I agree that the instruction booklets that come with electrical products sometimes contain so much detail that they simply cause confusion.

137:17:0.q: Why is it better to advance step by step when learning a foreign language rather than try to progress too quickly?
137:17:0.a: The reason it’s better to advance step by step when learning a foreign language rather than try to progress too quickly is that it’s impossible to absorb high-level language unless you can use language from lower levels easily and without thinking.
